data.title: The History of Australia: First Nations, Colonisation & Resistance (1770–1901)
data.description: From 65,000 years of continuous First Nations custodianship and Captain Cook’s voyage to the First Fleet, frontier wars, convict labour, the Gold Rush, and Aboriginal resistance, investigate how colonisation built modern Australia through dispossession and struggle.
data.synopsis: Sixty-five thousand years of the world's oldest continuous living culture collided in 1788 with eleven British convict ships casting anchor in Sydney Cove. Step beyond the colonial myth of terra nullius to discover the profound cosmology, complex diplomatic systems, and sophisticated fire-stick land management of First Nations peoples. Confront the brutal realities of convict transportation, the iron-fisted governance of penal colonies, and the fierce resistance of warriors like Pemulwuy during the Frontier Wars. From the blood-soaked Black War in Van Diemen's Land and the miners' democratic insurrection at the Eureka Stockade to the birth of a federated Commonwealth in 1901—explore the enduring story of invasion, resistance, and unbroken Indigenous survival.
data.enquiry: Invasion, Settlement, or Survival? How did British colonisation transform Australia?

data.synopsis: Armed merchantmen braving uncharted oceans, chartered monopolies extorting immense wealth from the Mughal Empire, and the catastrophic human horror of the Transatlantic Slave Trade. Confront the reality of the Middle Passage, the fierce guerrilla defiance of Queen Nanny and Jamaican Maroons, and the explosive rebellion of the Thirteen Colonies—as tea was cast into Boston Harbor and George Washington shattered imperial rule to ignite the American Revolution.

data.title: KS3: The Industrial Revolution (1750–1900)
data.synopsis: Steam engines shrieking in smoke-choked valleys, red-hot iron rolling through Henry Cort's puddling furnaces, and coal-fired textile mills driving the heartbeat of the modern world. data.synopsis: Before the catastrophic rupture of the Second World War, over nine million Jewish people inhabited every corner of Europe, speaking dozens of languages and enriching the intellectual, artistic, and political fabric of the continent. data.synopsis: Torn apart by two simultaneous existential struggles, the United States fought a ferocious battle for its own soul at home and abroad. Topeka and MLK's non-violent marches to the fiery radicalism of Malcolm X and Black Power. Simultaneously, deep in the Southeast Asian jungle, over 500,000 conscripted GIs waged a brutal counter-insurgency against resilient Vietcong guerrillas. As napalm, the 1968 Tet Offensive, and the My Lai massacre were beamed into American living rooms, anti-war protests, student strikes, and the Kent State shootings fractured the nation, culminating in painful withdrawal and the fall of Saigon in 1975.
